title: SQL Tables and Constraints: Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on defining relational tables: CREATE TABLE, data types, the five constraints, foreign key delete behaviour, and ALTER TABLE, ending with a sample schema and cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Tables and Column Definitions
points: A table is a named set of typed columns; each row is one record, and the schema (column names, types, constraints) lives in the database catalog
CREATE TABLE name (col type [constraints], ..., [table constraints]); IF NOT EXISTS skips the error when the table already exists
Column constraints sit inline after the type; table constraints sit at the end and are required for multi-column keys
Example: CREATE TABLE users (id INT PRIMARY KEY, email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP);
DROP TABLE removes structure and data; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS avoids the error, and TRUNCATE empties rows but keeps the structure

chapters.title: Choosing Data Types
points: Integers: SMALLINT (2 bytes), INT (4 bytes, about 2.1 billion max), BIGINT (8 bytes); use BIGINT for ids that may outgrow INT
Exact decimals: DECIMAL(p,s) or NUMERIC(10,2) for money; FLOAT/DOUBLE are approximate, so 0.1+0.2 is not exactly 0.3
Text: CHAR(n) is fixed-length and space-padded, VARCHAR(n) is variable with a max length, TEXT is unbounded
Dates: DATE (day only), TIME, TIMESTAMP (date and time; store in UTC), plus BOOLEAN for true/false flags
Mistake: storing money in FLOAT, or dates as VARCHAR, which breaks sorting, comparison and date arithmetic

chapters.title: PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE and NOT NULL
points: PRIMARY KEY = UNIQUE + NOT NULL, identifies each row, and a table has at most one; it automatically gets an index
Composite key: PRIMARY KEY (order_id, product_id) is a table constraint and uniqueness applies to the combination, not each column
UNIQUE allows many per table and permits NULL (in most databases multiple NULLs are allowed because NULL is not equal to NULL)
Auto ids: id INT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY (standard SQL/Postgres), AUTO_INCREMENT (MySQL), AUTOINCREMENT (SQLite)
NOT NULL rejects missing values; mistake: forgetting it on required columns, since a column without it accepts NULL even if the app assumes otherwise

chapters.title: FOREIGN KEY and ON DELETE
points: FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id) forces every child value to match an existing parent key or be NULL
The referenced column must be a PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE, and both columns must have the same data type
ON DELETE CASCADE deletes child rows with the parent; SET NULL nulls the child column (it must be nullable); SET DEFAULT uses the column default
ON DELETE RESTRICT blocks the delete at once; NO ACTION (the default) blocks it at statement end and allows deferral in some databases
Mistakes: CASCADE on important data silently wipes related rows; SQLite needs PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON; index the FK column since joins and parent deletes scan it

chapters.title: CHECK, DEFAULT and ALTER TABLE
points: CHECK (price >= 0) rejects any row where the condition is false; a NULL result passes, so combine with NOT NULL
DEFAULT supplies a value when the column is omitted from INSERT: status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'active'; DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP is common
Name constraints for clear errors and easy drops: CONSTRAINT chk_price CHECK (price >= 0)
ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN c type; DROP COLUMN c; RENAME COLUMN a TO b; ALTER COLUMN c TYPE type (Postgres) or MODIFY COLUMN (MySQL)
ALTER TABLE t ADD CONSTRAINT name ...; DROP CONSTRAINT name; mistake: adding NOT NULL to a populated column with no DEFAULT fails, and adding a constraint can lock a large table

chapters.title: Sample Schema and Cheat Sheet
points: users(id PK identity, email UNIQUE NOT NULL, created_at DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
orders(id PK, user_id FK REFERENCES users ON DELETE CASCADE, total DECIMAL(10,2) CHECK (total >= 0), status DEFAULT 'pending')
order_items(PRIMARY KEY (order_id, product_id), order_id FK ON DELETE CASCADE, product_id FK ON DELETE RESTRICT, qty INT CHECK (qty > 0))
Create parents before children and drop children before parents, otherwise the FK blocks the statement
Cheat sheet: PK = UNIQUE+NOT NULL | UNIQUE allows NULL | FK needs a PK/UNIQUE target | CASCADE deletes, SET NULL nulls, RESTRICT blocks | CHECK passes on NULL | DECIMAL for money
